notes.title: Monday Musings #7 – Blooming Community
notes.content:
Designing a fantasy factory game means walking a careful line: we want MoteMancer to feel unique, but not unfamiliar. And this week, we’re celebrating one of the best parts of development — [b]feedback that helps the game bloom.[/b]

[h3]🌿 The Challenge: Early Power Puzzles[/h3]

In MoteMancer, Life power spreads through a living network of [b]Mana Roots[/b] and [b]Mana Blooms[/b] — a branching, organic system instead of traditional power poles. That’s by design. We want power to feel like something you grow.

But after chatting with some of our early testers, a pattern emerged:
[list]
[*] New players felt confused or limited by the lack of “traditional” power poles.
[*] [b]Veterans[/b] quickly worked around the system before Mana Bloom even unlocked, making it feel like a tool you didn’t really need anymore.
[*] The [i]fantasy[/i] of growing a living network was there — but the [i]timing[/i] was off.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/f89e8a4087b3ac8f77b3cb423f93d213b7902d75.png[/img]

[h3]🧪 The Solution: Community-Nurtured Sprouts[/h3]

So we talked. We tried things. And we grew into something better. 🌸

Now, [b]Mana Bloom unlocks earlier[/b] — right alongside Mana Roots — giving you a clearer sense of how these two tools complement each other. Instead of feeling like a late-game patch, Bloom is now part of your foundational power puzzle.

And to really bring it to life?

[h3]🌱 New Upgrade: Rampant Bloom[/h3]
[b]“Mana Blooms extend their root network under adjacent Production Structures.”[/b]

This upgrade changes everything:
[list]
[*] Larger structures spread Bloom further.
[*] You still have to solve logistics, but now with more [i]creative flexibility[/i].
[*] It enhances Life’s identity — [i]grow a living, sprawling grid[/i] — instead of erasing the puzzle with raw range.
[/list]
Could we have just made Mana Bloom’s radius bigger? Sure. But that would’ve removed gameplay. This upgrade adds it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/e7af30493152c940fcbc1b6e240a1f4ab28214e2.jpg[/img]

[h3]🎉 Thank You, Testers[/h3]

A huge shoutout to the testers and players who helped shape this direction. MoteMancer is better because of you. This has already inspired designs that will improve the rest of the game as well!

Stay tuned — the [b]public demo is almost here[/b], and we can’t wait to see the wild ways you grow your power network. 🌞

Thanks for reading! See you next Monday for another MoteMancer Musing.

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: Monday Musings #6 – Elemental Aspects
notes.content:
In MoteMancer, power doesn’t just flow through wires or roots — it flows through [i]you[/i].
This week, we’re exploring [b]Aspects[/b] — elemental stances that shape how you interact with the world.

While Spells are short bursts of active magic (we’ll cover those in a future post), Aspects are [b]persistent auras[/b] that shift your role while building. They’re mutually exclusive — you can only channel one at a time — but each offers a unique way to approach a challenge, solve a puzzle, or accelerate your expansion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/dbbbf4758c2e8fbd36eef85383613c307ce5a389.png[/img]

[b]Biorhythm[/b] – The Builder’s Breath
Using your own latent energy, Biorhythm powers up nearby structures — perfect for establishing an outpost before local logistics and power are fully solved. It can also jumpstart a system that just needs a little push to become self-sustaining.

[b]Levitate[/b] – Crawl, Walk, Soar
Some Motes lie just out of reach. Levitate lets you cross chasms, slip between cliffs, and access resource patches that would otherwise require a lengthy detour.

[b]Wavedash[/b] – Ride the River
Streamways aren’t just for ingredient transport — with Wavedash, they become highways. Surf the elemental current and traverse your base faster than walking would ever allow.

[b]Excavator[/b] – Dig, Harvest, Rebuild
Need to reshape your setup fast? Excavator accelerates deconstruction and harvesting. The more you harvest in succession, the faster you get — sliding into the flows of refactoring.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/d29ac96fba76611cd85495f9f2bbb8838c43aa7b.png[/img]

The challenge with designing Aspects isn’t just making useful powers — it’s making sure they [i]feel[/i] elemental. Each one is meant to evoke the essence of its plane, and while you’ll likely find yourself drawn to a favorite that fits your playstyle, each tool in the right circumstance can make all the difference.

Later we’ll touch on [b]Spells[/b] — dramatic, momentary bursts of magic like Daycaller or Meteor Swarm. But for now, consider how you’d shape the world… if you could only take one form at a time.

Thanks for reading! We’ll see you next Monday for another MoteMancer Musing. 
Comment below on Aspects or spells that align with your inner Elemental flow or spells you hope to uncover in your interplanar journey. ✨

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: Monday Musings #5 – Smoke and Mirrors
notes.content:
Up until now, I’ve been a little quiet about my love for FX and math, but they’ve definitely been a driving force behind MoteMancer—both in gameplay and aesthetics. Today, we’re going to take a deep dive into some of the clever tricks that make this game’s visual style uniquely its own.

[b]The Challenge[/b]
A lot of factory-style games use 3D models or animated flipbooks for their visual effects. But, for MoteMancer, there’s a catch: the game is predominantly 2D, built on a hex grid, and filled with so many unique structures that the texture load would become overwhelming. So, what’s an FX nerd to do?

[b]A Clever Solution: Custom UV Maps[/b]
One of the most fascinating tricks up an FX artist's sleeve is manipulating UVs. UVs are typically used to map textures onto 3D meshes, but with the right math, you can use them to simulate all sorts of effects — even things that look like 3D objects, like spheres, wheels, or flowing rivers. It’s all about precision and a little custom shader code.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/7dc8428b70de5a1b1a2e86f6f8d67c259ebd196d.png[/img]

Rather than rely on bulky 3D models or animated textures, I’ve used this technique to create the illusion of depth and motion, even in a 2D space. The Grindstone and Streamways featured in the images below were particular challenges, but custom UV maps saved the day. It’s one of those tricks that makes MoteMancer’s aesthetic stand out — clean, beautiful, and deceptively efficient.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img]

🔮 [b]Grindstone[/b] – The Grindstone spins with motion and texture, thanks to custom UV manipulation. It’s a neat little illusion that helps this otherwise flat 2D structure feel dynamic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/c19dd8e6c2928e6b91bcf0e38b0785af91917ec6.gif[/img]
💧 [b]Streamways[/b] – The flowing, river-like effect you see here is also achieved through UV manipulation. No need for complex meshes or flipbook textures — just a few math tricks and a dash of shader magic.

The most exciting part of all this is that it’s not just about looking good — they help maintain performance. With so many unique structures and environments in MoteMancer, efficiency is key, and the trick of faking 3D with UV manipulation means we can have depth and motion without the extra texture load.

[b]And That’s Just a Taste[/b]
The possibilities with UV manipulation are endless. You can create anything from shifting slabs to swirling storms, all without the hefty resource cost of 3D meshes or massive sprite sheets. While you won’t always see the magic happening in the background, each illusion helps MoteMancer feel more alive and vibrant. It's the kind of thing I love about game development: painting with math.

Thanks for reading! We'll be back next Monday with another MoteMancer Musing.
Until then, may your Grindstones spin true and your Streamways flow forever. ✨

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: Monday Musings #4 – Salt, Aether, and the Heart of Alchemy
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/06dafa33f06ba05e43fbb27a149e9c4576da70bb.png[/img]
Most automation games have some form of processing:
Iron ore becomes iron plates. Rocks become bricks. Coal keeps the fire burning.

But in [i]MoteMancer[/i], we don't need coal.
We have [b]Salt[/b]. And we have [b]Aether[/b].

Today’s topic: [b]the catalysts that power your alchemy[/b].

🧂 [b]Salt and the Foundation of Matter[/b]
In MoteMancer, [b]Salt[/b] isn’t just something you dig out of the ground — it’s the residue of elemental persistence.

[b]Water[/b], [b]Earth[/b], and [b]Shadow[/b] Motes can be [b]ground[/b] into Salt.
These Motes anchor themselves to the world, sinking deep, condensing into crystals that stabilize your earliest tools and constructs.

Salt becomes the catalyst that sculpts the world's foundation into usable forms — and the backbone of your journey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/2337ae99459a72ca77658d30bc285fdd5bcf2a4f.png[/img]
💨 [b]Aether and the Breath of Change[/b]
Where Salt is weighty and tangible, [b]Aether[/b] is the light that dances between moments.

[b]Life[/b], [b]Fire[/b], and [b]Air[/b] Motes can be [b]drawn[/b] into Aether — distilled from raw vitality, flame, and breath. Aether is not mined or harvested; it is coaxed, captured, and refined.

It floats. It weaves. It binds. And with it, you’ll unlock the secrets of harnessing elemental forces beyond the material world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/bca14dd299b71b0f302ff5130d894049c8ce8212.png[/img]
🔮 [b]Catalysts, Choices, and Evolution[/b]
Every Mote Field you encounter is a living decision.

Will you [i]grind[/i] the Motes into Salt and use them to strengthen your structures?
Or will you [i]draw[/i] their essence into Aether, enabling deeper transmutations?
And the Motes themselves, when bound to their neighboring catalyst, [b]become fully formed[/b], unlocking their true elemental nature.

Your relationship to the land will evolve as you do. Some planes are rich in Motes that favor Salt, others in Motes that sing with Aether — and learning to read the world around you is key to survival, expansion, and discovery.

And when Salt and Aether finally combine?
They form [b]Salt Prisms[/b] — crystalline keys that power all [b]research[/b], [b]advancement[/b], and [b]exploration of the unknown[/b].

[b]This is the heart of MoteMancer’s alchemy: a living, breathing puzzle, shaped by your choices and the world's whispering secrets.[/b]

Thanks for reading! We'll be back next Monday with another MoteMancer Musing.
Until then, may your Salt shine bright and your Aether flow free. ✨

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: Monday Musings #3 – The Shape of the World
notes.content:
It’s Easter week — a fine time to talk about [i]finding things in unexpected places.[/i]
In MoteMancer, you won’t be hunting for eggs… but you [i]will[/i] be following trails of glowing stones, mysterious terrain shifts, and overgrown pathways to discover the pieces you need to bring your magical masterpiece to life.

Today’s topic: [b]World Generation[/b].

There’s no grand overworld map in MoteMancer (at least, not yet). Instead, the world unfolds like a woven tapestry — meant to feel intimate, immersive, and filled with secrets waiting to be noticed.


🌱 [b]Mote Patches and Natural Bloom[/b]
Every resource in the world comes from the ground — literally.
[b]Motes[/b] are the source of all things: Trees, crystals, Emberboughs, Shadefangs… they all [i]burst forth[/i] from the elemental energy seeping through the soil.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/6b2501d5fc859e26dde8a4cb8691c28b3f873277.png[/img]
Each field leaves a subtle trail. Flora and crystals spawn in [b]three branching directions[/b], creating natural paths. See a trail of flowers stretching into the distance?
Follow it. It’ll lead you to a [b]field of Life Motes[/b].


🧱 [b]Terrain as Storytelling[/b]
Not every clue sprouts upward — some lie beneath your feet. When terrain shifts from natural (grass, sand) to something manmade (brickwork, tiles), you’re getting close to a [b]Planar Portal[/b].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/8565f093857e36bafc5777ced996f6fd045cfb1b.png[/img]
These ancient crafted paths wear their age differently depending on the plane: On the Life plane, you’ll find mossy, overgrown paths. On Water, those same bricks are buried beneath sand. 


✨ [b]A Seamless Connection Between Planes[/b]
One of the trickiest parts of designing the world was making [b]portal transitions[/b] feel grounded.
We wanted something elegant, diegetic, and flexible — and the answer turned out to be right beneath us.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/be432d4d253acc234b5161eba2a3b6004b31de86.png[/img]
The [b]manmade ground tiles[/b] appear on both sides of a portal, changing only in how they’ve been shaped by their environment. Once you learn to spot them, you’ll not only find portals — you might even guess which plane is on the other side before you step through.

Exploration in MoteMancer isn’t about fog-of-war — it’s about pattern recognition, world knowledge, and a touch of intuition. The motes will guide you. You just have to learn how to see them.

Thanks for reading! We’ll be back next Monday with another MoteMancer Musings.

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: Monday Musings #2 – The Nature of Power
notes.content:
When it comes to building a fantasy factory, you need two things:
Something to move the parts, and something to make them move.
Today, we’re diving into the second part — [b]Power[/b].

In MoteMancer, every plane has its own logic — and its own way of generating energy.
Thanks to the elemental system, you’ll always have access to [b]at least one power style[/b] on any plane, which means you get choices. And choices mean puzzles.

Unlike some factory games where placing power poles is just checking a box, we wanted [b]power to feel like part of the world[/b]. Each source ties directly into the elemental flavor of its plane — mechanically and thematically.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img]🌿 [b]Life: Solar, but organic[/b]
Life’s power system revolves around [b]Mana Leaves[/b] — solar-generating plants that bloom across the land.
The catch? You have to [i]grow[/i] your own living grid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/564bd03c170d9629642d389bb781d1e3216b3b35.png[/img]
Connect Mana Leaves using [b]Roots [/b]and [b]Blooms [/b]to carry energy where you need it. It’s free, flexible, and beautifully messy — like nature itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img]🔥 [b]Fire: Modular combustion[/b]
Fire’s power is fueled by Elemental Fire, and delivered through [b]Pedestals [/b]and lava.
Rather than fixed generators, you can shape your own lava networks using [b]Lava Barriers[/b] and [b]Fire Wire[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/cb4bfc212fcd8dffaec512ea72725a6c53e0b4ef.png[/img]
Additional Pedestals increase your burn rate, and each Pedestal gains efficiency for each surrounding lava tile. Whether you optimize for throughput, efficiency, or go full volcano-core aesthetic, the design is in your hands.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img]🌬️ [b]Air: Wind-powered precision[/b]
Air offers free energy like Life, though unpredictable. Water is a complimentary partner to Air and Life, offering the [b]Mana Pool[/b], a way to store energy when the winds die down or the sun sets.
Air power flows in narrow streams through structures called [b]Gust Funnels[/b], blowing energy across the map in directional bursts, offering the most range for spreading power, but confined to a single-width line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/758462ee92393e340cd8a21c435100a7bb2d250c.png[/img]
Gale Generators give you more power when placed in open space — and planning your wind corridors becomes a puzzle of its own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img]
✨ [b]Mana Flare: Your first spark[/b]
Every MoteMancer starts with a simple spell: [b]Mana Flare[/b].
It’s small, temporary, and handy in a pinch — casting a burst of energy that powers nearby structures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/798018142ec309dc19d1742e611638ea62914ed6.png[/img]
Eventually you’ll outgrow it, but it’s more than just a stepping stone. Through research, it evolves — unlocking upgrades like Tectonic Flare, which scans for nearby portals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/54037ec78f081302d9ae52ac2fe3bb25ea6bc0d7.png[/img][b]Power isn’t just fuel in MoteMancer — it’s an expression of the world itself.[/b]
And with six elemental planes to explore, there’s plenty more power to uncover.

Thanks for reading! We'll be back next Monday with another MoteMancer Musing.
Until then, may your Lava flow strong and your Leaves reach the sun. 🌞

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]

notes.title: MoteMancer Musings #1 – Speaking the Language of Alchemy
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings, MoteMancers![/h1]
The elemental current flows strong this week.

When you make a game about smelting iron and assembling widgets, the language mostly speaks for itself. Steel beams go into factories. Bolts come out. Players know what to expect.

But when you swap out coal for Aether and circuits for Brimstone... things get a little weirder.

MoteMancer is a fantasy automation game set across six elemental planes — from the molten boughs of Fire to the creeping tendrils of Shadow. It’s a fantasy-rich setting, but one that doesn’t always come with a ready-made vocabulary. There’s no cultural shorthand for what a “Verdant Collector” does, or how “Mana Roots” propagate Power. And that means we have to work harder to ensure it all [i]feels[/i] intuitive.

Which brings us to this week’s milestone: [b]localization.[/b]
We’ve begun the process of translating [i]MoteMancer[/i] into 14 languages, and it’s already clear just how much thought went into every single word.

We’re not aiming for ornate fantasy prose — the goal is natural, evocative language that melts into your play session. It should spark a feeling, deliver meaning quickly, and then vanish like mist. If you remember a line, it’s because it nestled somewhere between your puzzle-solving brain and your inner poet.

Here’s a small taste of what that looks like in-game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45567834/a30d56c4dc4bfbc9a4fc96738a0cce9d6b0efc48.png[/img]

You’ll see this style woven throughout the game — from ingredients to structures to characters. It's concise but vivid, aiming to stir imagination without slowing down the moment-to-moment play.

We also shared our intent with the localization team directly. Here’s an excerpt from the letter we sent them:

[quote][i]“Our goal is to make each word do as much work as possible — evoking alchemy, elemental forces, and player comprehension all at once. You'll find the language often walks a tightrope: concise but evocative, grounded but mystical…”[/i] [/quote]

Translation isn’t just about finding equivalents — it’s about carrying that emotional weight across cultures. We deeply believe that the game’s themes — growth, balance, elemental identity — are universal. And we want as many players as possible to feel like this world was written just for them.

If we do our jobs right, it’ll all [i]feel[/i] intuitive — even if no one’s ever played a fantasy factory game before.

—

Thanks for reading. We’ll be back next Monday for another [b]MoteMancer Musing[/b].
Until then: may your Leaves be plentiful, and your Roots well-tended. 🌿

[b]— The MoteMancer Team[/b]
